$comment: Run learnings (crew src/learnings): when a run ends with evidence worth learning from (the operator's rulings, standing steers, the orchestrator's decisions, a reviewer's findings, a check that was red on the base or ran out of time), crew launches this one-seat, one-turn run on a seat that did NOT build the run (the builder never grades itself). It reads the handoff crew wrote (the evidence, what is already proposed) and writes report.json; crew files each learning in the approve queue as a memory proposal attributed to the SOURCE run. Nothing is used until a person approves it. Cheap by design: no repository, nothing built, no floor, no judge (required_instruments is [] on purpose: a person judges each proposal).
title: Distill learnings
summary: Turns what a finished run went through into a few durable learnings, proposed for your review.
use_when: A run just ended and its record holds rulings, steers, decisions or review findings worth keeping

phases.instructions: You distil learnings; you never file them. Read the handoff file named in the task. It names the source run, its repository, `evidence` (each item: id, kind, text) and `already_proposed` (learnings already in the review queue), and report_path (the ONE file you may write). Keep only what passes the durability test: would this help a fresh session, on a different task, three months from now? Each kept learning states the rule, why it holds, and when it applies, in 1 to 3 plain sentences, and names its repository when it is about one. Good learnings: a test or check that fails under host load and why; a sandbox or seat limitation and its workaround; a repository rule or convention that bit; a pattern a reviewer flagged that would recur; a decision with its reason when it constrains future work; a standing preference the operator stated. Drop: progress or status (what was done, merged, shipped), anything only true of this one change, run ids, PR or issue numbers, commit SHAs, dates, and anything already in already_proposed. Never invent: every learning must be supported by an evidence item, and you name those ids. Write report_path as one JSON object: {"learnings": [{"kind": "gotcha|decision|pattern|steering", "content": "<1 to 3 sentences>", "evidence": ["<evidence ids>"]}]}, at most 5 entries, best first. An empty list is a valid and common answer. Do not open, edit or run anything else: no repository, no tool that writes, no proposals (crew files those). Write report_path before you finish and end your reply with its absolute path.
